## Course Overview

Theory of sampling distributions; principles of data reduction; point and interval estimation; sufficient statistics; order statistics; hypothesis testing; correlation and linear regression; introduction to linear models.

## Planned Topics

The outline follows the Spring 2026 course. Textbook selection and assessment policies will be confirmed for Spring 2027.

- **Introduction and Probability Review:** Statistical inference; populations, samples, distributions, and convergence.
- **Estimation and Confidence Intervals:** Point estimation, sampling distributions, confidence intervals, sufficiency, and optimality.
- **Hypothesis Testing:** Likelihood ratio tests, error probabilities, power, and asymptotic inference.
- **Linear Models:** Least squares, inference, diagnostics, ANOVA, and extensions.

## Provisional Prerequisites and Objectives

The Spring 2026 course expected multivariate calculus, linear algebra, calculus-based probability, comfort with proofs, and comfort with code. These prerequisites await confirmation for Spring 2027.

Planned objectives carried forward for review are to:

- distinguish population characteristics from sample estimates;
- use probability as the basis for statistical inference;
- evaluate estimators and hypothesis tests;
- construct and interpret confidence intervals;
- understand when asymptotic approximations are appropriate;
- use Python or R for statistical computation; and
- communicate statistical analyses through explanatory text, tables, and graphs.
